annotations.title: Find software or post a buyer request

description: Best first call when a user wants software to license, white-label or resell. Describe the need in plain words: returns the best matching listings with why they fit, plus a ready buyer-request draft. If nothing fits (or the user wants sellers to come to them), call again with post=true and buyer_email: the buyer confirms by email, matching sellers are emailed and reply on LicenseSaaS. No account or key needed. Show the user the draft and get their OK before posting.

agent_key.description: Optional: a key from register_agent or Account settings -> Agent keys. With a key the request goes live at once, from that account.

buyer_email.description: No agent_key? The buyer's email. We email them a link and the request goes live when they click it (nothing is published before). Ask your user for it and tell them to expect the email.

client_name.description: Your assistant's name, e.g. "Claude", shown in the buyer's confirmation email.

need.description: The user's need in plain words, 20-3,000 characters, e.g. "white-label AI chatbot we can resell to dental clinics in the UK, about $300 a month".

post.description: true to post the request (after the user approved the draft). Needs buyer_email or agent_key.

request.description: Optional: the request_draft from a previous call, edited with the user.

deal_types.description: How they want to use it: white_label (rebrand as their own), license (use it), reseller, partnership, or any.

description.description: Details in the buyer's words, 20-5,000 characters: use case, must-haves, who it's for. No contact details or links.

primary_category.description: Category value from get_buyer_request_schema, e.g. "crm-sales". Leave out if unsure.

request_type.description: Older single-value form of deal_types; still accepted.

target_territory.description: Where it will be used or sold, e.g. "UK".

title.description: What the buyer needs, 8-160 characters, e.g. "White-label CRM for real estate agencies".

name: find_or_request
